item: grave labels drifted across the three gravedigger lanes (c1 FOSSIL; c2 DONE-ELSEWHERE/SUPERSEDED-BY/STILL-RELEVANT; c3 ABSORBED-BY/STILL-RELEVANT/FOSSIL); build one stable vocabulary: tools/grave_classify.py (canonical five-label set, handoff path + optional successor hint, label + one-line justification, exit 2 on unknown labels) plus tests/test_grave_classify.py
note: Canonical set locked at exactly five: FOSSIL, ABSORBED-BY, SUPERSEDED-BY, DONE-ELSEWHERE, STILL-RELEVANT. Tool is 284 lines, generic, deterministic, never fabricates: decision order is explicit --label, then marker scan of the file (md Verdict/classification lines and json fields; unknown marker token = exit 2 drift enforcement, multiple distinct canonical markers = exit 3), then --successor found on disk defaults SUPERSEDED-BY (pass --label ABSORBED-BY to mean absorption), then STILL-RELEVANT with an unclassified-by-evidence note (age reported as data, never a verdict). Missing handoff or ghost successor = exit 1. My own tests caught 3 defects pre-fix (formatting chars before FOSSIL token, leading brace on json fields, successor default never wired); fixed and re-run green.
